Vitamin D deficiency in the elderly may be less prevalent in the USA, due to fortification of food.1 Food fortification has there- fore been recommended,1 or supplementation with doses in the region of 10 to 20 micrograms (400 to 800 units) daily;1,4 20 micrograms (800 units) daily is considered necessary for re- duction of falls and fractures in the elderly.2,7,11 The 2005 Dietary Guidelines for Americans recommend that elderly people should consume 25 micrograms (1000 units) daily; the upper level of 50 micrograms (2000 units) should not be exceeded.5 See also Osteomalacia, and Osteoporosis, below. 1.
